implementation_notes.anchor: For each pair, --anchor-sft 1.0 back-propagates 1.0 x model(**VLCollator(processor, assistant_only=True)([to_chat(processor, row, 'ref')])).loss / grad_accum on the policy's chosen pass. This is the response-only CE on row['ref'] = refs[i][0], the image's first human caption, which equals P1's SFT target (prompt and response) on all 1,000 RL images (checked by --check). Gradients add, so each update equals one with run_dpo's loss + 1.0 x CE. There is no NLL on the chosen caption. run_dpo's logged loss is the DPO term; each pair's CE and DPO margin go to pairs_log.jsonl
implementation_notes.token_kl: --token-kl 0.4 (A-KL) replaces the anchor with the sum, over the chosen response's tokens (assistant-only positions), of the full-vocabulary KL(pi_SFT || pi_theta), divided by the batch size (1). pi_SFT is the frozen ref_sft adapter. This follows HALVA's L_d: github.com/pritamqu/HALVA llava/train/halva_trainer.py lines 585-590 at commit ce52b7022eca40a73b4110950b80a548598aadec ('divergence = ref*(log ref - log pol)', masked, '.sum()/batch_sz'; 'loss = alignment_loss + self.loss_alpha*divergence'). Settings: lr 2.5e-6, the same pairs and settings otherwise, its own 20-pair dry run first
implementation_notes.akl_trigger: A-KL runs iff arm A failed G2 or G3 (s3_gate.akl_triggered, which needs only the dev decode). Any guard failure makes the verdict KILL, so this equals the registered 'KILL and G2 or G3 failed'. The selftest asserts that the verdict is KILL whenever the trigger fires. s3_verdict.json shows arm A's verdict, its failed guards and the A-KL verdict together; A-KL's verdict replaces A's
implementation_notes.reference: The DPO reference must be pi_SFT (run_dpo's ref_sft adapter = runs/p1dev_s42). A base-anchored fallback is refused before training
implementation_notes.dpo_checkpoints: run_dpo has a hand-written loop, and the committed hook patches only the HF Trainer, so train_stage2_anchor.py writes OUT/checkpoint-<step> every 200 optimizer steps itself. Each holds the trainable weights, the AdamW state, the RNG states and the per-pair log, written atomically. Each is mirrored to /root/outputs/runs/<run>, keeping 2 (the hook's RESCAP_* settings and layout). A rerun resumes from the newest: the same seeded shuffle, minus step x grad_accum pairs. resume_manifest.json records resumed_from_step in the hook's format. The selftest shows that a resumed run's weights and log are bitwise equal to an uninterrupted run's. The SFT arm (train_stage2.py) is checkpointed by the committed hook. Only the last checkpoint is evaluated
implementation_notes.dry_run: train_stage2_anchor.py --dry-run trains run_dpo's --limit 20 (the first 20 rows of dpo.jsonl). It passes iff gradients flow at the first regulariser backward and at the first optimizer step, and peak reserved <= 22 GB (torch.cuda.max_memory_reserved()/1e9, train_rl.py's unit). The verdict is written into train_summary.json's dry_run block, and a failed dry run blocks the job on every rerun. The pair-ordering accuracy is logged
implementation_notes.ordering_accuracy: Computed over every trained pair from the per-pair margins (the float32 arithmetic of run_dpo), so it survives a resume. The selftest checks it against run_dpo's own per-type count
implementation_notes.panel: data/ktvic_openviic_refs.json is git-excluded. s3_gate.py reads it only to derive per-image classes (objects_in), checks its sha256 and the 296 dev images, and writes no caption text. If it is absent on the GPU machine, every other number is computed, and a verdict that depends on panel_cm is PENDING_PANEL (computed by trying both sides of the bound). The same pinned s3_gate.py --verdict is then rerun where the panel is, writing a new --out
implementation_notes.cm_rft_tie_break: CIDEr-D against references 1-4: rl_reward.CiderD with document frequencies from all 5 references of each of the 3,469 train-minus-dev300 images, tokens from rl_reward.Reward (RDRSegmenter, lowercase, as evaluate.py). This is a reading of 'train-minus-dev300 document frequencies'. The 'pool index' is the index of a sample's first occurrence among the 12 (T 0.5 then T 0.8)
implementation_notes.copy_guard: An exact copy is a greedy caption whose rl_reward.Reward copy statistic has smallest word edit distance 0 to one of the image's 5 references (segmented content words). Rates are counted on the first 250 RL ids in schedule order, for the arm (its own decode of those images) and for P1_dev (its decode of the 1,000 RL images, restricted to those 250)
implementation_notes.decodes: evaluate.py, short prompt, greedy, bf16, its defaults: dev300 via NCS_DATASET=ktvic_dev (ktvic_dev_split.py --json-dir); RL images via NCS_DATASET=ktvic_s3rl with rl1000_data.json and rl250_data.json (s3_gate.py --prep: the RL images' train references in KTVIC's layout). Predictions are kept, so a scoring failure is re-scored and never re-decoded
implementation_notes.pool_resume: e5_sample.py appends and skips the images already written. Its RNG is seeded once at start, so after a restart the remaining images' samples differ from an uninterrupted run's. A resume is logged in events.log
implementation_notes.estimators: s3_gate.py reproduces the registered P1_dev values from the committed n2 decode: P 74.291, R 43.126, F1 54.572, m 1.7633, residual +0.17, panel F1 40.653 on 296 images. Paired percentile bootstrap: indices numpy default_rng(0).integers(0, n, (2000, n)) and np.percentile 2.5/97.5, as rl_reward.boot, recomputing object_prf.scores and the frontier residual per draw. count-matched estimators keep the images with the same number of distinct classes in the arm and P1_dev and report the matched share
implementation_notes.never_overwrite: Every output is written once: an identical rewrite is a no-op and anything else is refused (write a _v2). Each job step is skipped when its output exists, and SHA256SUMS gets _vN names
implementation_notes.provenance: Every JSON written by these scripts embeds the committed hook's machine_id, git_head_sha, checkpoint_resume_hook_sha256 and train_stage2_sha256, plus the shas of the five files above; the DPO runs also record train_stage2_anchor_sha256 and resumed_from_step. evaluate.py's outputs get the hook's .provenance.json sidecars, and the job stamps $O at the end

self_tests.s3_gate.py --selftest: PASS (53 s). Covers: (1) pair construction through cm_pairs.build: count match, |dsyl| <= 2, TP(w) >= TP(l) + 1, empty/CJK/function-word-end/copy filters, dedup, CAP 4 with the largest dTP first, ref = refs[0], determinism; (2) the verdict table on its boundaries for A, AKL and R, including the panel-absent cases; (3) H5 (amendment 1): clause 1 only, clause 2 only, both, neither (HOLDS and NOT_SHOWN), dR_UB = 0, dP_LB = 0, dR = 0; (4) the estimators against hand-derived P, R, F1 and residual; (5) synthetic data whose verdicts come from the data: a fixed-count TP gain PASSES, a count rise KILLs through G1, no change KILLs, no panel gives PENDING_PANEL or KILL; G2-G6 on their boundaries; an A-KL trigger implies KILL; (6) the --verdict report end to end, without and with A-KL
self_tests.cm_rft.py --selftest: PASS. Covers: count match, the TP rule, the filters, the CIDEr and pool-index tie-breaks, the 1:1 rows, the merge order
self_tests.train_stage2_anchor.py --selftest: PASS. Uses the real train_stage2.run_dpo on a toy two-head model and a processor that expands the image placeholder only in __call__, like Qwen2.5-VL's. Per-pair anchor CE and token KL equal hand-derived values (1e-5), and the accumulated gradients equal a hand-derived autograd of sum[-logsigmoid(beta x margin) + alpha x term] / grad_accum (allclose 1e-6/1e-5). The DPO margins and run_dpo's own ordering accuracy agree. Resume after a simulated crash is bitwise equal (resumed_from_step [2]; 2 checkpoints kept in OUT and in the mirror). The dry run's pass follows its rule. Refused: a finished run, two regularisers, a base-anchored reference, SFT
self_tests.mutation_probes: Local only, not committed. 10 mutants were all caught. In s3_gate: the two strict H5 bounds, panel_lo >, d_res_lo >, G6 <=, and count matching switched off. In train_stage2_anchor: the anchor on the chosen caption, the legacy mask, no / grad_accum, and a mean instead of a sum for the KL
